descriptors.concept_name: Mode Of Taking Or Accepting Certain Loans, Deposits And Specified Sum [Section 269Ss]
descriptors.definition: Accepting loans, deposits, or specified sums equal to or exceeding 20,000 rupees must be executed through account payee cheques, bank drafts, electronic clearing systems, or prescribed electronic modes. Specified sums include advance monies receivable regarding immovable property transfers, subject to specific institutional exemptions and agricultural conditions.
inclusion: Loans or deposits of 20,000 rupees or more
Unpaid earlier loans or deposits aggregating 20,000 rupees or more
Specified sums receivable for immovable property transfers
exclusion: Transactions involving the Government or banking companies
Transactions where parties derive income solely from agriculture
Transactions where neither party has taxable income
nearby_distinctions: Differs from Section 269T which governs loan repayments rather than acceptance
Differs from Section 269ST which governs general daily or transactional cash receipt limits

descriptors.definition: Receiving an amount of 2,00,000 rupees or more is prohibited unless executed through account payee instruments, electronic clearing systems, or prescribed electronic modes. This restriction applies to daily aggregates from a single person, single transactions, or transactions relating to a single event or occasion.
inclusion: Receipts of 2,00,000 rupees or more in aggregate from a person in a day
Receipts of 2,00,000 rupees or more in respect of a single transaction
Receipts relating to one event or occasion from a person
exclusion: Receipts by the Government, banking companies, post office savings banks, or co-operative banks
Transactions of the nature referred to in section 269SS
Cash withdrawals by any person from a bank, co-operative bank, or post office savings bank
nearby_distinctions: Differs from Section 269SS which specifically targets loans, deposits, and immovable property advances
Applies a higher monetary threshold of 2,00,000 rupees compared to the 20,000 rupees limit under Section 269SS and Section 269T

descriptors.concept_name: Facility For Accepting Payment Through Prescribed Electronic Modes [Section 269Su]
descriptors.definition: Businesses with total sales, turnover, or gross receipts exceeding 50 crore rupees in the preceding financial year must provide facilities for accepting payments through prescribed electronic modes. Non-compliance attracts a daily penalty under section 271DB, while system providers are prohibited from imposing charges for using these mandated modes.
inclusion: Businesses with gross receipts exceeding 50 crore rupees
RuPay debit card payment facilities
BHIM-UPI and BHIM-UPI QR code payment facilities
exclusion: Assessees whose gross receipts do not exceed the 50 crore rupee threshold
Specified persons having exclusively B2B transactions with at least 95 percent non-cash receipts
nearby_distinctions: Mandates the provision of electronic payment acceptance facilities rather than restricting transaction modes like sections 269SS, 269ST, and 269T

descriptors.concept_name: Mode Of Repayment Of Certain Loans Or Deposits [Section 269T]
descriptors.definition: Banking companies, co-operative banks, companies, firms, and other persons are prohibited from repaying loans, deposits, or specified advances of 20,000 rupees or more except via account payee cheques, bank drafts, electronic clearing systems, or prescribed electronic modes. This rule evaluates aggregate outstanding balances or specified advances held on the repayment date, including interest.
inclusion: Repayment of loans or deposits aggregating 20,000 rupees or more
Repayment of specified advances totaling 20,000 rupees or more
Higher limit of 2,00,000 rupees for primary agricultural credit societies and primary cooperative agricultural and rural development banks
exclusion: Repayments made by crediting the amount directly to the recipient's savings or current bank account
Repayments of loans, deposits, or advances taken from the Government, banking institutions, or statutory corporations
nearby_distinctions: Mirrors the restrictions in Section 269SS but explicitly governs the repayment phase of loans, deposits, and specified advances rather than their initial acceptance

descriptors.definition: Asset transfers executed by an assessee during or after tax proceedings before service of recovery notices are deemed void against tax, penalty, or interest claims exceeding 5,000 rupees. However, transfers made for adequate consideration without notice of pending proceedings or executed with prior Assessing Officer permission are valid, provided the assets do not form stock-in-trade.
inclusion: Sales, mortgages, gifts, exchanges, or other asset transfers during tax proceedings
Asset values exceeding 10,000 rupees with tax liabilities exceeding 5,000 rupees
exclusion: Transfers made for adequate consideration without notice of proceedings or tax liabilities
Transfers executed with the prior written permission of the Assessing Officer
Transfers of assets representing the stock-in-trade of the business
nearby_distinctions: Deems completed asset transfers void post-proceeds to protect revenue recovery, whereas Section 281B empowers pre-emptive property attachment during ongoing proceedings

descriptors.concept_name: Provisional Attachment To Protect The Interest Of The Revenue [Section 281B]
descriptors.definition: Assessing officers are empowered to provisionally attach an assessee's property during pending assessment, reassessment, or penalty proceedings with high-ranking administrative approval to protect revenue interests. Such attachments remain valid for six months, extendable up to two years or sixty days post-assessment, but can be revoked if the assessee furnishes a scheduled bank guarantee.
inclusion: Provisional attachment of property during pending assessment or reassessment
Attachments for anticipated penalty under section 271AAD exceeding two crore rupees
Revocation of attachment upon furnishing a scheduled bank guarantee
exclusion: Extensions exceeding a total period of two years or sixty days after assessment/reassessment, whichever is later
nearby_distinctions: Acts as a precautionary attachment mechanism during active proceedings, distinct from Section 281 which retroactively voids fraudulent transfers

descriptors.definition: Tax communications, notices, and summons may be served by post, approved courier services, Code of Civil Procedure methods, electronic records, or other CBDT-prescribed transmission means. Specific statutory addressees are designated for serving notices corresponding to distinct entity types such as firms, Hindu Undivided Families, companies, and associations.
inclusion: Service by post or approved courier services
Service via electronic records under IT Act chapter IV
Designated addressees for firms, companies, HUFs, and local authorities
exclusion: Unapproved non-statutory communication channels lacking CBDT backing
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on the procedural modes and mandatory recipient addressees for serving notices, whereas Section 282A governs the authentication and signing validity of those notices

descriptors.concept_name: Authentication Of Notices And Other Documents [Section 282A]
descriptors.definition: Notices and documents issued by income-tax authorities must be properly signed and issued in paper form or authenticated electronically via prescribed procedures to support paperless assessments. Electronic communications are deemed authenticated when issued from designated email addresses or displayed on designated websites with the authority's name and office printed or displayed.
inclusion: Notices in e-mail bodies bearing printed name and office from designated addresses
Notices contained in attachments of emails issued from designated addresses
Electronic records displayed on designated websites containing name and office details
exclusion: Communications failing to use designated email addresses or lacking printed authority identification
nearby_distinctions: Governs the digital and paper-form authentication requirements of issued documents, whereas Sections 282 through 284 regulate the physical and electronic transmission channels and recipient addressees

descriptors.concept_name: Submission Of Statements By Producers Of Cinematograph Films Or Persons Engaged In Specified Activity [Section 285B]
descriptors.definition: Producers of cinematograph films and persons engaged in specified activities must furnish an electronic statement in Form No. 52A within 60 days from the end of the financial year. This filing covers aggregate payments exceeding 50,000 rupees made to persons engaged in production, event management, documentary creation, or television and OTT programming.
inclusion: Producers of cinematograph films
Persons engaged in event management, documentary production, or television/OTT programming
Payments exceeding 50,000 rupees in aggregate to engaged persons
exclusion: Aggregate payments to a person not exceeding the 50,000 rupee threshold
Activities outside the defined scope of film production or specified event and media management
nearby_distinctions: Targets industry-specific production and event management reporting under Section 285B, whereas Section 285BA imposes general financial transaction reporting obligations across financial institutions and reporting entities

descriptors.concept_name: Obligation To Furnish Statement Of Financial Transaction Or Reportable Account [Section 285Ba]
descriptors.definition: Specified entities, including reporting financial institutions, registrars, and government offices maintaining books or records, must furnish statements regarding specified financial transactions or reportable accounts to income-tax authorities. These prescribed transactions encompass property purchases, service rendering, works contracts, investments, expenditures, and loan takings.
inclusion: Transactions of purchase, sale, or exchange of goods, property, or rights
Transactions for rendering services or under works contracts
Transactions involving investments made, expenditures incurred, or loans taken
exclusion: Entities outside the designated categories of reporting persons and financial institutions defined under the section
nearby_distinctions: Imposes broad financial transaction reporting obligations across designated institutional entities, whereas Section 285B is strictly confined to film producers and specified media/event activities

descriptors.definition: Tax authorities must upload an annual information statement in Form No. 26AS into an assessee's registered electronic filing portal account within three months of receiving the underlying data. This statement aggregates information on tax deducted or collected at source, specified financial transactions, tax payments, demands, refunds, and pending or completed proceedings.
inclusion: Information relating to tax deducted or collected at source
Information relating to specified financial transactions and tax payments
Information relating to demands, refunds, and pending or completed proceedings
exclusion: Data outside official authority possession or information not authorized for upload under relevant tax exchange agreements
nearby_distinctions: Constitutes the consolidated statement uploaded to the taxpayer's portal under Section 285BB, whereas Section 285BA governs the underlying reporting obligations submitted by reporting entities

descriptors.definition: The Central Government may publish an assessee's name, address, and proceeding details in the public interest, along with partner or director particulars for firms and companies. However, penalty or prosecution publications are restricted until appeal periods expire without filing or until filed appeals are fully disposed of.
inclusion: Publication of assessee name, address, and proceeding particulars in public interest
Publication of names of partners, directors, or managers for firms and companies
Publication after appeal windows expire or appeals are disposed of
exclusion: Penalty or prosecution publications made while appeal rights remain active and unexpired
nearby_distinctions: Authorizes public disclosure of assessee particulars by the government under Section 287, whereas Sections 287A and 288 regulate professional representation and appearance before tax authorities and tribunals
